Extract values from netCDFs to one or more point observations

Source: R/extract_to_points.R
extract_to_point.Rd

This is the general point-extraction interface. It can extract environmental values for one or multiple observations. The user chooses the type of extraction with the method argument. The more specific functions extract2d(), extract3d_surface(), extract3d_bottom(), extract3d_nearest() and extract3d_all() are wrappers around this function.

Usage

extract_to_point(
  data = NULL,
  nc,
  lon = NULL,
  lat = NULL,
  depth = NULL,
  date = NULL,
  var = NULL,
  method = c("2d", "surface", "bottom", "nearest", "all"),
  lon_col = "lon",
  lat_col = "lat",
  date_col = "date",
  depth_col = "depth",
  id_col = NULL,
  file_col = "file",
  lon_dim = NULL,
  lat_dim = NULL,
  depth_dim = NULL,
  time_dim = NULL,
  time_match = c("nearest", "exact"),
  max_time_diff = NULL,
  output_prefix = NULL,
  output_col = NULL,
  verbose = FALSE,
  time_resolution = c("auto", "datetime", "daily", "monthly", "yearly", "custom"),
  custom_time_interval = NULL,
  time_report = TRUE,
  spatial_match = c("within", "nearest"),
  max_distance_km = NULL,
  spatial_report = NULL,
  depth_report = NULL
)

Arguments

data

Optional object containing observation points. Can be a data frame, tibble, sf object with POINT geometries, matrix with column names, or named list. If NULL, coordinates can be supplied directly through lon, lat, and optionally depth and date. For sf objects, longitude and latitude are obtained from the POINT geometries; projected geometries are transformed internally to longitude and latitude when a CRS is available.

nc

netCDF source. Can be a file path, vector of file paths, list of file paths, opened ncdf4 object, list of opened objects, or a data frame with a file column.

lon

Optional numeric longitude value or vector for direct point extraction when data = NULL.

lat

Optional numeric latitude value or vector for direct point extraction when data = NULL.

depth

Optional numeric observation depth value or vector for direct point extraction. Required when data = NULL and method = "nearest" or method = "all".

date

Optional observation date or vector of dates for direct point extraction. Used when data = NULL and the netCDF variable has a time dimension. Accepts Date and POSIXt objects, or character values in "YYYY-MM-DD" or "YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS" format (UTC). Direct input vectors may have length 1 or a common compatible length.

var

Name of the variable to extract from the netCDF file. If NULL, the function tries to detect the variable automatically from each file. This only works when each netCDF file contains one single variable.

method

Extraction method. Options are "2d", "surface", "bottom", "nearest" and "all". With method = "all", the function returns nearest, surface and bottom outputs together.

lon_col

Name of the longitude column in data.

lat_col

Name of the latitude column in data.

date_col

Name of the date column in data. Required only when the netCDF variable has a time dimension.

depth_col

Name of the observation-depth column in data. Required only when method = "nearest" or method = "all".

id_col

Optional observation identifier column. It is not required for extraction, but it is checked when provided to help users detect mistakes.

file_col

Column containing file paths when nc is a data frame.

lon_dim

Optional name of the longitude dimension in the netCDF file.

lat_dim

Optional name of the latitude dimension in the netCDF file.

depth_dim

Optional name of the depth dimension in the netCDF file.

time_dim

Optional name of the time dimension in the netCDF file.

time_match

Character. How observation dates are matched to netCDF time values. "nearest" (default) selects the closest available date; "exact" requires an exact date match and returns NA when no match exists.

max_time_diff

Optional non-negative numeric value giving the maximum allowed difference, in days, between an observation date and the nearest netCDF date when time_match = "nearest". If NULL (default), no maximum temporal distance is imposed. Ignored when time_match = "exact".

output_prefix

Optional name used for the extracted output column. If omitted, var is used.

output_col

Optional alias for output_prefix. Use this when you want to define the exact name of the output column directly. If both output_col and output_prefix are provided, output_col is used. With method = "all", this name is used as the suffix in nearest_*, surface_* and seabottom_* columns.

verbose

Logical. If TRUE, progress messages are printed every 100 rows.

time_resolution

Precision used to compare observation times with dataset timestamps. "auto" uses daily comparison for Date objects and date-only text, and datetime comparison for POSIXt objects and date-time text. Explicit alternatives are "datetime", "daily", "monthly", "yearly" and "custom". Calendar comparisons use UTC. These options compare timestamp labels; they do not infer averaging intervals or calculate temporal summaries. Multiple dataset records mapping to the same comparison value cause an error. With nearest matching, monthly and yearly comparisons use the start of the labelled month or year. max_time_diff remains in days and applies to these comparison values. Use exact matching to require the same labelled day, month or year.

custom_time_interval

Positive difftime value used as the warning interval when time_resolution = "custom". Matching uses full timestamps. This interval does not reject candidates; use max_time_diff for that.

time_report

Logical. If TRUE, the default, display a temporal summary when returned values are displaced in time, or outputs are missing for a temporal reason (no timestamp within the matching settings, or no observation date for a source with a time dimension). Outputs missing because of location or depth are reported by spatial_report and depth_report instead. The return format is unchanged. FALSE hides the summary but does not suppress temporal warnings.

spatial_match

Horizontal selection rule. "within" (default) requires the point to lie inside a cell. "nearest" selects the geographically closest cell centre, including outside the grid, up to max_distance_km. The rule applies equally to one or multiple sources. A selected missing value does not trigger a search for another cell in the same source.

max_distance_km

Required finite non-negative distance in kilometres when spatial_match = "nearest". Distance is the great-circle distance from the observation to the cell centre on a sphere of radius 6371.01 km (the radius sf::st_distance() uses with s2), and does not depend on sf settings. A cell exactly at the limit is accepted. Must be NULL with "within".

spatial_report

NULL (default) reports missing spatial outputs and selections of cells that do not contain the requested point. TRUE also reports normal and exact selections; FALSE hides the spatial report.

depth_report

NULL (default) reports missing depth outputs, selections more than one local layer spacing away, and displaced singleton layers whose spacing cannot be assessed. TRUE also reports normal surface, bottom and exact depth selections; FALSE hides the depth report. Depths are in metres, positive down. Report modes do not change returned values.

Value

If data is provided, the input observations with extracted values appended. Data frames, tibbles and sf objects retain their structure; matrices and named lists are returned as data frames. If data = NULL, direct extraction returns a numeric value for one point and one output, a numeric vector for multiple points and one output, a named numeric vector for one point and multiple outputs (for example, method = "all"), or a data frame for multiple points and multiple outputs.

Details

Numeric netCDF time coordinates must provide units expressed as milliseconds, seconds, minutes, hours or days since a reference date-time. Singular and plural unit names are accepted.

Reference date-times are interpreted in UTC. A trailing "Z" or "UTC" is accepted; numeric timezone offsets such as "+02:00" are not currently supported.

Supported calendars are "standard", "gregorian" and "proleptic_gregorian". The first two are supported only for reference dates and timestamps on or after 1582-10-15. Unsupported units, calendars or missing time units produce an error.

Temporal resolution controls comparison of timestamp labels. It does not identify averaging intervals, calculate temporal means, or interpret climatological periods.

Physical depth coordinates

Observation depths must be in metres, positive downward (0 at the surface); negative observation depths are rejected, and depths in other units must be converted first. Dataset coordinates are converted from m, meter(s), metre(s), km, kilometer(s), kilometre(s), cm, centimeter(s) or centimetre(s). The positive attribute determines direction when supplied; height and altitude axes without it are read as positive-up. Otherwise uniformly non-negative values imply positive-down and non-positive values imply positive-up. Mixed signs without direction metadata are rejected. The depth coordinate must have units, including for surface and bottom extraction; a file with a single depth level can be read with extract2d(). Surface means the physically shallowest layer, even if its value is missing. Bottom means the deepest non-missing layer. Nearest selects the valid layer closest to the observation depth; ties select the shallower layer. Selection does not depend on the storage order of the depth coordinate. Duplicate physical depths, unsupported units, coordinates above the assumed reference surface, and sigma, formula-based or pressure coordinates require explicit correction or conversion before extraction.

Multiple sources

Spatial matching uses the same rules for one or multiple sources. With spatial_match = "within", only cells containing the point are eligible. With spatial_match = "nearest", the requested point may be outside grid coverage. The nearest cell centre must be within max_distance_km of it. Explicit spatial cell bounds are preferred. Otherwise, or when the bounds variable is missing or invalid (with a warning), edges are inferred from adjacent centres; singleton axes without bounds require coincidence, up to single-precision rounding of the stored coordinate. Longitude comparisons support equivalent coordinates across the antimeridian. A point on an edge shared by two cells uses the first cell in storage order. Among eligible sources the closest temporal candidate with a valid value wins. With "within" matching, equal temporal distances are resolved by input order, so list the preferred source first. With "nearest" matching, they are resolved by geographic distance to the cell centre (differences under 1 m are ignored), then by input order. Existing output columns are replaced, including by NA. Output names cannot overwrite extraction inputs or combine different variables in the same column.

Custom temporal intervals

With time_resolution = "custom", observations require hours as for datetime. For example, custom_time_interval = as.difftime(3, units = "hours") warns above three hours of displacement. Exact matching requires the same timestamp. Auto matching remains unchanged and uses the observed cadence for diagnostics.

Spatial and depth reports

The default NULL mode reports only missing outputs, selected cells that do not contain the requested point, and unusually distant depth selections. TRUE requests a full report, including normal and exact selections; FALSE hides the corresponding report. Returned values are identical in all modes. Spatial reports show the requested point, selected cell centre, distance and any explicit distance limit. With within matching, a point may be inside a cell without coinciding with its centre. Depth reports describe physical layers in metres, positive down from the reference surface. Surface means the shallowest layer; bottom means the deepest layer with a valid value, not an independently measured seabed. Values are selected without vertical interpolation. Normal nearest-depth approximations are silent in automatic mode. A difference strictly greater than the local layer spacing is reported. Spacing uses the two physical layers surrounding the requested depth, including layers with missing values. At an exact layer, its nearest neighbour defines the spacing; outside the range, the two nearest edge layers are used. Singleton axes have no spacing to assess a nonzero displacement. Messages identify the reference layers and only attribute a displacement to missing values when closer physical layers must lack valid values under nearest-valid selection. Missing outputs are explained once, with rejection reasons for each relevant source; a repeated reason is shown once with up to three of its files. The cause is taken from the sources whose grid covers the point, unless none does. Temporal causes (including a missing observation date) are reported by time_report; spatial and depth causes by their corresponding switches, so FALSE hides them. Mixed causes are grouped under spatial first, then depth, then time, with all reasons shown. Reports count distinct observations and output values separately. At most five cases are shown, prioritising missing values; truncation and the count omitted are stated. Coordinates use up to five decimals; metres/kilometres normally use up to two. Extra decimals distinguish values close to a limit when rounding would otherwise make them appear equal. Calculations retain full precision. Small positive distances use <0.01 rather than zero. Depth comparisons in reports allow a relative tolerance of 1e-6, so single-precision depth axes match their nominal depths.

Temporal diagnostics

Diagnostics are emitted after source selection, for values actually returned. Daily, monthly and yearly comparisons warn on a change of calendar period in UTC. Datetime comparisons warn when displacement exceeds one observed cadence step, or when a nonzero displacement has no reliable cadence. With a detected daily cadence, datetime comparison also warns when the selected value falls on a different UTC day, even below 24 hours. Explanatory warnings include the requested and selected timestamps, their difference, the comparison resolution, cadence, row, variable and file name. Reports explain non-warning displacements and missing outputs without repeating examples already explained by a temporal warning. Cadence inference does not change matching or impose a maximum time gap. Singleton sources may use the observed sequence of compatible files for the same variable. Time bounds describe intervals, not sampling frequency.

Examples

nc_file <- system.file(
  "extdata", "example_3d.nc",
  package = "ocean3d"
)

# Extract the value closest to a single observation
extract_to_point(
  nc = nc_file,
  lon = 0,
  lat = 40,
  depth = 60,
  date = "2020-01-03",
  var = "temp",
  method = "nearest"
)
#> [1] 15.5

# Extract values for multiple observations
extract_to_point(
  nc = nc_file,
  lon = c(0, 1),
  lat = c(40, 41),
  depth = c(60, 100),
  date = "2020-01-03",
  var = "temp",
  method = "nearest"
)
#> [1] 15.5 13.5

# Match a complete observation timestamp.
# The example file has a reading at midnight on 2020-01-03.
extract_to_point(
  nc = nc_file,
  lon = 0,
  lat = 40,
  depth = 60,
  date = as.POSIXct("2020-01-03 00:15:00", tz = "UTC"),
  var = "temp",
  method = "nearest",
  time_resolution = "datetime",
  max_time_diff = 30 / 1440
)
#> Warning: Temporal warning: 1 observation(s) need attention.
#> 
#> A different timestamp was selected, but its cadence is unknown.
#> Row 1; variable: temp; output: temp.
#> Observation: 2020-01-03 00:15:00 UTC
#> Selected data: 2020-01-03 00:00:00 UTC
#> Difference: 15 minutes earlier.
#> Comparison resolution: datetime.
#> Detected cadence: irregular; no reliable sampling interval.
#> The available timestamps do not establish a reliable sampling interval. The time difference cannot be assessed against a detected cadence. Use time_resolution = 'custom' with custom_time_interval if you know the appropriate warning interval.
#> File: example_3d.nc
#> [1] 15.5

# Horizontal matching: this point is outside the example grid's cell edges.
# The default within rule returns NA; nearest accepts a centre within 60 km.
extract_to_point(
  nc = nc_file, lon = -0.6, lat = 40, date = "2020-01-03",
  var = "temp", method = "surface", spatial_match = "within"
)
#> Spatial selection: 1 observation had no value extracted.
#> 1 output value affected; 1 missing.
#> 
#> Row 1 · netCDF variable: temp · output column: temp
#> Point outside cell coverage (within matching).
#> File: example_3d.nc
#> Result: NA.
#> [1] NA
extract_to_point(
  nc = nc_file, lon = -0.6, lat = 40, date = "2020-01-03",
  var = "temp", method = "surface", spatial_match = "nearest",
  max_distance_km = 60
)
#> Spatial selection: 1 observation outside cell coverage used the nearest cell.
#> 1 output value affected.
#> 
#> Row 1 · netCDF variable: temp · output column: temp
#> Requested: (-0.6, 40) → nearest cell centre: (0, 40)
#> Distance: 51.11 km; allowed: 60 km.
#> File: example_3d.nc
#> [1] 20.5

# Report modes do not change the extracted value.
# NULL is automatic: the normal nearest-depth approximation stays silent.
automatic <- extract_to_point(
  nc = nc_file, lon = 0, lat = 40, depth = 60, date = "2020-01-03",
  var = "temp", method = "nearest",
  spatial_report = NULL, depth_report = NULL
)
# TRUE explains the selected cell and depth, including normal selections.
detailed <- extract_to_point(
  nc = nc_file, lon = 0, lat = 40, depth = 60, date = "2020-01-03",
  var = "temp", method = "nearest",
  spatial_report = TRUE, depth_report = TRUE
)
#> Spatial selection: 1 observation matched the requested selection.
#> 1 output value reported.
#> 
#> Row 1 · netCDF variable: temp · output column: temp
#> Requested: (0, 40) → containing cell centre: (0, 40)
#> Distance: 0 km.
#> File: example_3d.nc
#> Depth selection: 1 observation matched the requested selection.
#> 1 output value reported.
#> 
#> Row 1 · netCDF variable: temp · output column: temp
#> Requested: 60 m → selected: 50 m (10 m shallower).
#> No vertical interpolation.
#> Surrounding layers: 50–100 m (50 m apart).
#> File: example_3d.nc
# FALSE hides informational reports; temporal warnings remain active.
quiet <- extract_to_point(
  nc = nc_file, lon = 0, lat = 40, depth = 60, date = "2020-01-03",
  var = "temp", method = "nearest",
  spatial_report = FALSE, depth_report = FALSE, time_report = FALSE
)
identical(automatic, detailed)
#> [1] TRUE
identical(automatic, quiet)
#> [1] TRUE

# Compare monthly labels when the file has one record per month.
# Here the timestamp labels are illustrative.
monthly_labels <- as.Date(c("2020-01-15", "2020-02-15"))
observation_date <- as.Date("2020-02-28")
format(monthly_labels, "%Y-%m") ==
  format(observation_date, "%Y-%m")
#> [1] FALSE  TRUE

# For extraction from such a file, use:
# time_resolution = "monthly", time_match = "exact".
# Multiple records in the same month cause an error;
# they are not averaged automatically.
